plan.title: Liver treated vs control descriptive DE (no replicates)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a 1 treated vs 1 control bulk RNA-seq liver comparison from salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 3 samples in the file, but the metadata table confirms the design is 1 vs 1 with no biological replication). With no within-group replicates, DESeq2 cannot estimate a dispersion, so no inferential p-value has statistical grounding (per the knowledge service's flagged rule R-0003). The plan therefore: (1) runs sample-structure QC to confirm the samples group as expected and to check library size/composition, (2) filters low-count genes and computes DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors for normalization, (3) computes descriptive, unshrunken log2 fold changes between the single treated and single control sample on the normalized counts (no Wald test, no adjusted p-values, no LFC shrinkage — shrinkage and multiple-testing steps are dropped per the knowledge service because they require a fitted dispersion), (4) annotates gene symbols against the human organism package, (5) runs an over-representation analysis of the genes with the largest descriptive fold changes against WikiPathways/Reactome/MSigDB Hallmark human gene sets, explicitly using the tested genes as the universe, and (6) reports everything with an explicit statement that this design supports no inferential DE claim and describes what a replicated design would require. The DE step is a descriptive fold-change ranking, not a validated differential expression test — the report must say so plainly throughout.
